content_html:
Quantum I Ching — Structural Isomorphism

Isomorphism here is structural, not historical: the I Ching and quantum mechanics independently formalize a binary, dynamic logic of change where complementary opposites coexist as potential until observation selects an outcome. The resemblance arises from cognitive convergence (human reasoning via contrasts), shared binary combinatorics (2<sup>n</sup> states), and a common geometry of transformation (rotation/balance), not from direct influence.

Binary foundations: Yin (0) and Yang (1) lines combine into 64 hexagrams (26), mirroring a 6-qubit Hilbert space with 64 basis vectors.
Potentiality → outcome: Casting a hexagram parallels measurement collapse; intention/measurement context determines which state manifests.
Dynamics: Yi (change) corresponds to unitary evolution; transformations are rotations within a state space (Taiji circle ↔ Bloch sphere).
Complementarity: The unity of opposites (☯) anticipates Bohr’s complementarity—mutually exclusive yet jointly necessary descriptions.
Cognitive convergence: Independent traditions discovered similar structures because minds model uncertainty and change through binary contrasts and recursive composition.

Level I Ching Quantum Mechanics Shared Structure
Basis Yin (0) / Yang (1) |0⟩ / |1⟩ Two-state system
Combinatorics 64 hexagrams (2×trigrams) 2

basis states		 Binary vector space

Notes:

Structural, not causal: No claim that one system derived from the other; both formalize change under uncertainty.
Trigrams as basis: Each 3-line trigram maps to a 3-qubit computational basis state; stacking yields hexagrams (6-qubit space).
Geometry of balance: Yin–yang “rotation” (balance/phase) is analogous to qubit phase on the Bloch sphere.
